name: Reaction-network and gene-regulation structural analogy
summary: A bounded comparison of network motifs that transfer as structural language, not as biochemical identity.

source_domain.name: chemistry
source_domain.description: Chemical reaction networks with species, reactions, and rate-dependent flows.

target_domain.name: biology
target_domain.description: Gene-regulatory networks with genes, regulatory interactions, and expression states.

source_concepts.name: reaction node
source_concepts.description: A reaction event connecting input and output species.

source_concepts.name: species state
source_concepts.description: A concentration or presence state for a chemical species.

target_concepts.name: regulatory event
target_concepts.description: A regulatory interaction that changes expression activity.

target_concepts.name: expression state
target_concepts.description: An expression level or activity state for a gene.

correspondences.rationale: Both can be represented as directed transformations in a network model.
Both expose a domain-specific state variable whose value can change over time.

scale.description: Network-motif scale; this does not map individual molecules to individual genes.

shared_properties.name: directed interaction structure
shared_properties.description: Nodes and directed interactions can describe local influence or transformation structure.

preserved_properties.name: local connectivity
preserved_properties.description: The comparison preserves adjacency and direction as a question for motif analysis.

non_preserved_properties.name: mechanistic law
non_preserved_properties.description: Chemical kinetics and transcriptional regulation do not share the same parameters or governing laws.

counterexamples.description: A matching directed motif can have different rate laws, feedback delays, and stochasticity.
counterexamples.implication: Do not infer a shared simulation or prediction from the graph resemblance.

non_equivalence.statement: The source and target concepts are not the same entities or mechanisms.
